deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the manuscript of Riemann's 1857 fragment 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', published posthumously in his Werke. Systems (y_1,...,y_n) of multivalued functions belong to the same 'Klasse' if they have the same branch points a,b,...,g and the same monodromy substitutions (A),(B),...: a positive loop of x around a sends the column (y) to A·(y) with constant A. The theorem being finished on this page is the first Lehrsatz. It says that any n+1 systems y^(0),...,y^(n) of the same class satisfy linear relations (2): a_0 y_i^(0) + a_1 y_i^(1) + ... + a_n y_i^(n) = 0 for i=1..n, with a_k that are polynomials (entire rational functions) in x.

Step 1 (completion of the proof). By Cramer's rule the a_k are proportional to the signed n×n minors D_k of the n×(n+1) matrix [y_i^(k)]. Each D_k is a determinant of n systems of the class. By the previous page, each D_k is multiplied by det(A) under a loop around a. It is also O((x-a)^{μ̄_k}) there, so D_k = P_k(x)·(x-a)^{μ̄_k}(x-b)^{ν̄_k}...(x-g)^{ρ̄_k} with P_k a polynomial. Since all D_k acquire the same factor det A = e^{2πi μ̄_k}·(integer-power ambiguity), the exponents μ̄_k for different k differ by integers; likewise at b,...,g. Hence the ratios D_k/D_0 are rational functions of x. Clearing denominators [my gloss], one may take a_0,...,a_n to be polynomials in x, which proves the theorem.

Step 2 (derivatives). If a loop around a sends (y) to A(y) with A constant, then differentiating gives (y') → A(y'). Hence (dy_1/dx,...,dy_n/dx) is again a system of the same class, and so is each higher derivative system (y^(k)).

Corollary 1: apply the theorem to the n+1 systems (y),(y'),...,(y^(n)). Each y_i then satisfies a_0 y + a_1 y' + ... + a_n y^(n) = 0 with polynomial a_k, i.e. an n-th order linear ODE with polynomial coefficients. Implicitly a_n ∝ Wronskian W(y_1..y_n) ≠ 0 (assumes linear independence).

Corollary 2: apply the theorem to (Y),(y),(y'),...,(y^(n-1)) for any system Y of the same class. This gives c_0 Y_i = b_0 y_i + b_1 y_i' + ... + b_{n-1} y_i^(n-1) with polynomial c_0, b_k. Here c_0 is (up to sign) the Wronskian of y_1..y_n, so it depends only on y. Thus Y is expressed linearly in y and its first n-1 derivatives with rational coefficients.

Step 3 (announced program). Using Corollary 2, he investigates how far a system is determined by its 'Characteristik' (substitutions plus exponents). For any Y with the same substitutions and exponents as y, one gets (in Lagrange's prime notation) the n linear equations written out on the next page.
errors: No outright errors. Implicit assumption: the systems are linearly independent (nonvanishing determinant/Wronskian). Without it, a_n in Corollary 1 or c_0 in Corollary 2 could vanish identically. Riemann's previous page handles this by the clause 'wenn die Function nicht identisch verschwindet'.

The claim that exponents in the different minors 'offenbar' differ by integers is justified because each minor picks up the same factor det(A) under the loop. Determinacy of exponents mod 1 by det(A) is left implicit but is correct.
Corollary 2 states 'rationale Coefficienten'. Strictly, the coefficients are polynomials divided by the fixed polynomial c_0, which is consistent with the statement.

results.what: n+1 function systems of the same monodromy class satisfy a linear relation with polynomial coefficients; proof via Cramer minors whose monodromy factor is the common det(A)
results.modern_name: Rationality of ratios of Wronskian-type minors; linear dependence over C(x) of solutions with common monodromy (Riemann's first Lehrsatz)

results.what: Derivatives of a system form a system of the same class, since the monodromy matrices are constant
results.modern_name: Differentiation commutes with monodromy (horizontal sections / D-module structure)

results.what: Every class (given monodromy and branch points) of n-function systems satisfies an n-th order linear ODE with polynomial coefficients
results.modern_name: Existence of a Fuchsian-type ODE with prescribed monodromy given a solution system (precursor of Riemann–Hilbert problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857; Fuchs 1866 for the systematic theory of regular singular equations

results.what: Every system of the same class is a C(x)-linear combination of y, y', ..., y^(n-1)
results.modern_name: Cyclic vector / module of solutions with given monodromy is generated by one system over C(x)[d/dx]; contiguity relations generalized

deep.surprise_reason: This is the manuscript of Riemann's well-known 1857 fragment on linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients, printed in his Gesammelte Werke. The content is known and attributed to him; only manuscript-level details (deletions, wording) add anything.

checkable.sympy: x,a,b=symbols('x a b'); y1=x**a; y2=x**b; M=Matrix([[y1,diff(y1,x),diff(y1,x,2)],[y2,diff(y2,x),diff(y2,x,2)]]); a0=M[:,[1,2]].det(); a1=-M[:,[0,2]].det(); a2=M[:,[0,1]].det(); simplify(a0*y1+a1*diff(y1,x)+a2*diff(y1,x,2))
checkable.asserts: Signed Cramer minors give coefficients of a 2nd-order ODE annihilating y1 (result 0); same holds for y2.
The ratios of minors are rational in x even though the minors themselves carry non-integer powers of x, i.e. the ODE is x^2 y'' + (1-a-b) x y' + a b y = 0 (both expressions 0).
Differentiation commutes with a constant monodromy matrix, so the derivatives form a system of the same class (zero vector).
A system Y (here x^(a+1),x^(b+1), same monodromy as x^a,x^b) is c0^{-1}(b0 y + b1 y') with c0 the Wronskian and b0,b1 rational in x.
